# The independent CBOR implementation for the F14 / Q11 cross-check.
#
#   pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-crosscheck.txt
#
# Decision D7 §D12 pins the version; decision D31 pins the ROLE: cbor2 is a
# DECODE-only vehicle. The RFC 8949 §4.2.1 canonical ENCODER the cross-check
# compares against is our own, written in
# testdata/vectors/v1/crosscheck_cbor.py -- D31 §8 rejected
# cbor2.dumps(canonical=True) because its key order is RFC 7049 length-first,
# which only *coincides* with §4.2.1 over today's unsigned-integer keys.
#
# cbor2 is a DEV TOOL. It never enters any Rust dependency tree
# (docs/dependency-policy.md §5); the test
# `the_cbor2_pin_is_exact_and_dev_tool_only` refuses to let its name appear in
# a Cargo manifest. Contract: docs/testing/cbor-cross-check.md.
#
# Every artifact PyPI publishes for 6.1.3 is hashed here, so the pin holds on
# any platform CI or a contributor happens to use. cbor2 6.x is a compiled
# Rust/PyO3 extension with NO pure-Python fallback, which is why the wheels
# matter and why the sdist alone is not enough.

# Pip-less bootstrap table (pip ignores comments).
#
# Not every machine has pip -- the reference dev box has neither pip nor
# ensurepip. `scripts/cross-check.sh --setup` reads these rows, reconstructs
#   https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/<b2[0:2]>/<b2[2:4]>/<b2[4:]>/<name>
# (exactly what the PyPI JSON API returns), fetches the wheel for the running
# interpreter, verifies the SHA-256 against the row, and unzips it into a
# cache OUTSIDE the repo. A wheel is a zip, so no installer is required.
#
